subject: Can the number of significant digits for parameter sample output be increased (using CmdStan)?

messages.author: 0bf3f1057439abb9
messages.subject: Can the number of significant digits for parameter sample output be increased (using CmdStan)?
parts:
Hi all,
Sorry if this is a duplicate question. 

It looks like the number of significant digits in the output.csv from parameter samples in CmdStan is 6.  Can this be increased to get more precision for my external processing case?

Thanks!
REub

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can the number of significant digits for parameter sample output be increased (using CmdStan)?
parts:
You're unlikely to have more than six digits of accuracy
in any of the estimated quantities unless you have more
than 1e6 effect sample size.

Here's the usage you get if you don't supply arguments:

~/cmdstan(develop)$ bin/stansummary
USAGE: stansummary <filename 1> [<filename 2> ... <filename N>]

OPTIONS:

--autocorr=<chain_index> Append the autocorrelations for the given chain

--sig_figs=<int> Set significant figures of output (Defaults to 2)

--csv_file=<filename> Write output as csv file

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can the number of significant digits for parameter sample output be increased (using CmdStan)?
parts:
You can use sig_figs to report more digits in stansummary, but
I believe the original question was whether or not more digits
could be saved for each sample. That answer is no and, as
Bob notes, it would be dangerous to claim that having more
would be useful outside of some very extreme circumstances.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can the number of significant digits for parameter sample output be increased (using CmdStan)?
parts:
Sorry---misunderstood the question. We should have
a way to control the number of digits in our floating
point ASCII output. Best thing to do is come up with
a binary format in either single (4 byte) or double (8 byte)
precision. I created an issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/2245

- Bob
